summary: Olivia Chow consistently frames small business support as central to local job creation, affordability, and community vitality across both the 2014 and 2023 mayoral campaigns. Chow has pledged to fix CaféTO by shortening timelines, reducing costs, and giving operators more certainty, and has tied small business success to community land trusts and strong local economies. Earlier positions emphasized fighting unemployment through small businesses, creating 5,000 jobs for young people over four years, and expanding training and apprenticeships modelled on the Orlando Training Centre. Chow has also voiced support for fairness in the taxi industry, affordability for artists, the importance of arts and film, local journalism, and a $15/hour federal minimum wage. Documented actions include releasing a job creation platform, touring training facilities, and meeting directly with affected workers such as taxi drivers.

key_positions.stance: Supports small businesses as a tool to fight unemployment and grow local economies
Supports fixing the CaféTO program by shortening timelines, reducing costs, and creating more certainty for small businesses
Supports job creation for young people, including a target of 5,000 jobs over four years
Supports expanding training and apprenticeship programs, citing the Orlando Training Centre as a model
Supports making Toronto more affordable for artists and recognizes arts and film as important to the city's economy
Supports fairness for taxi drivers and the taxi industry
Supports community land trusts as a means for small businesses to thrive

key_actions.action: Released the first planks of a job creation and business platform focused on supporting small businesses
Toured the Orlando Training Centre as a model for an apprenticeship and training plan
Publicly questioned John Tory over a proposal to relocate 5,000 jobs out of Toronto
Met with taxi drivers from across Toronto to discuss industry concerns and fairness
Pledged to fix CaféTO by shortening timelines, reducing costs, and creating more certainty
